name: Raymond James Financial, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate, durable wealth franchise: recurring fee-based revenue on a record $1.15T of Private Client Group fee-based assets, a decades-old advisor platform with consistent net new asset growth, diversification across wealth/capital markets/asset management/banking, ~19% returns on common equity and steady buybacks — against the structural portability of advisors (clients follow the advisor, and Morgan Stanley/Schwab/Fidelity/large RIAs recruit aggressively), revenue geared to equity-market levels via AUM-based fees, rate-sensitive bank/sweep income exposed to cash sorting, and cyclical capital-markets revenue. No network effect or hard switching-cost lock-in.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 12 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Diversified wealth/capital-markets franchise, moat 6/10 — earnings power is real and current (record fiscal Q3 2026, ROE 18.8%), but the OCF-based OE model fits a broker-dealer/bank poorly and even generous growth only gets a 9.47% weighted IRR at $155.04 (IV@15% $80.54); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$81.
moat_for: Recurring fee-based revenue: record $1.15T PCG fee-based assets at Jun 30, 2026 — market appreciation converts to revenue without new sales
Advisor platform and brand trust since 1962; consistent net new assets ($21.7B domestic PCG in fiscal Q3 2026 alone)
Diversified across wealth, capital markets, asset management and banking — no single line carries the P&L
Disciplined capital return: share count CAGR −1.37%/yr, buybacks continuing ($400M in fiscal Q3 2026); strong regulatory capital (22.5% total capital ratio)
moat_against: Advisors can leave and take clients with them; rivals (MS, Schwab, Fidelity, large RIAs) recruit aggressively
Revenue geared to equity-market levels via AUM-based fees — a drawdown cuts the top line mechanically
Bank/sweep earnings are rate-sensitive; cash sorting already showed clients move balances for yield
Capital markets revenue is deal-cycle cyclical; no network effect or switching-cost lock-in
